title: [Chapitre] IV. Analysis situs (première mouture) : notes manuscrites (10/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the first draft of Grothendieck's axiomatic 'Analysis situs' (1986). This is the programme of 'tame topology' from the Esquisse, here treated as a lattice-theoretic or categorical axiomatics.

- There is a class of 'figures', ordered by ≤ (subfigure). Inside it sits a class M of 'multiplicités', i.e. irreducible pieces or closed (multi)strata.
- \bar F denotes the set of X ∈ M with X ≤ F, the closed strata of F.
- There is a relation X ≪ F between figures, roughly a morphism in a class 'Inj' of embeddings or refinement maps.
- For a subfigure Y of the target, F_Y denotes the induced subfigure ('image inverse') of the source.
- A stronger relation X ⋘ Y reads as 'X is carried by Y and does not fall into the boundary of Y'.
- The previous page states the Proposition. Let F be a figure and X ∈ M with X ≪ F. Then (a) there is Y ∈ M, Y ≤ F, with X ⋘ Y. (b) Among such Y there is a smallest one, characterised by the condition that the subfigure of X induced by ∂Y is ≠ X.
- Part (a) was proved on p.78. Write F = Sup Y_i; axiom C6 says inverse image commutes with Sup, so X = Sup F_{Y_i}. Since X is a multiplicity (irreducible), X = F_{Y_i} for some i.

This page proves (b).
1. Among Y ∈ \bar F with X ≪ Y, choose a minimal one. It exists because finite figures have finite combinatorial dimension, so descending chains are finite.
2. Minimality means: for every strict sub-multiplicity Y' < Y, X is not ≪ Y', i.e. F_{Y'} ≠ X.
3. Write ∂Y = ∪_{Y'∈M, Y'<Y} Y'. Applying C6 again together with the irreducibility of X, this is equivalent to F_{∂Y} ≠ X. This gives the characterisation of the minimal Y as 'X not induced from the boundary'.
4. Uniqueness / least element: let Y' ∈ \bar F with X ≪ Y', so F_{Y'} = X. Inverse images by Inj-maps preserve intersections: F_Y ∩ F_{Y'} = F_{Y∩Y'}. Hence F_{Y∩Y'} = X, so X factors through Y∩Y'.
5. Decompose Y∩Y' into multiplicities. Again by irreducibility, X factors through some Z ∈ M with Z ≤ Y∩Y' ≤ Y. Minimality forces Z = Y, so Y ≤ Y'. Hence Y is the least element.

Modern reading: this is the existence and uniqueness of the 'carrier' (support stratum or cell) of an irreducible piece under a refinement or embedding. It is the axiomatic analogue of 'the smallest closed simplex or stratum containing a given point or cell'. The next page uses it to define a monotone map of strata posets φ: \bar F → \bar G for F ≪ G, i.e. the carrier map of a subdivision or refinement.
errors: The final line concludes 'par suite Y = Y'', but the argument (and the stated goal 'prouvons que Y ≤ Y'') only gives Y ≤ Y∩Y' ≤ Y', i.e. Y ≤ Y'. Equality holds only if Y' is also minimal. This is a slip; the intended conclusion is Y∩Y' = Y, i.e. Y ≤ Y'.

Existence of a minimal element is justified only by an appeal to finite 'combinatorial dimension' of finite figures, which is not yet among the stated axioms. Grothendieck himself notes that a stronger dimensional minimality is available, so this step is a gap relative to the axiom list.
The characterisation in (b) is shown only in one direction: minimal ⇒ F_{∂Y} ≠ X. The converse (F_{∂Y} ≠ X ⇒ minimality) is implicit, via irreducibility plus C6, but is not written out.

ideas.what: Least multiplicity (stratum) Y of F carrying an irreducible X under a refinement/embedding, characterised by X not being induced from ∂Y
ideas.modern_name: carrier / support stratum (smallest closed cell or simplex containing a point or cell); carrier of a subdivision
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical combinatorial topology (Alexander, Whitehead-era simplicial and CW theory)
ideas.where_published: Analysis situs drafts unpublished; the tame-topology programme is sketched in Esquisse d'un programme §5

ideas.what: Inverse image along 'Inj' maps preserves intersections (F_Y ∩ F_{Y'} = F_{Y∩Y'}) and arbitrary Sups (axiom C6); irreducibility of multiplicities then forces factorisation through a single piece
ideas.modern_name: pullback along monomorphisms preserves meets; join-irreducible (prime) elements in a distributive lattice of closed subsets

ideas.what: Resulting monotone map between posets of strata, \bar F → \bar G, for F ≪ G (stated on the next page)
ideas.modern_name: induced map of stratification posets for a refinement; carrier map Sd K → K
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical; in stratified homotopy theory (exit-path categories) folklore

deep.surprise_reason: This is a routine lattice-theoretic lemma, the existence of a carrier stratum, inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatic tame topology. It is interesting only as a document of the axiomatic approach; the mathematics itself is classical and contains a minor slip.
transcription_corrections: 'on n'a pas X ≪ Y'' — the image shows ≪ with a slash, i.e. 'on a X ≪̸ Y''; the transcription's '\not\ll' inside 'on n'a pas' double-negates. The intended meaning is that X ≪ Y' fails.
'pour Y' [multiplicité] strict de Y' likely reads 'pour Y' multiplicité stricte' / 'sous-multiplicité stricte de Y'.
Formula under ∂Y: ∂Y = ∪_{Y'∈M, Y'⊊Y} Y' (written as subscripts 'Y'∈M, Y'≤Y', strict); the crossed-out first attempt is 'Y'⊊Y'.
'(appliquant à nouveau (C6))' — the reference is to axiom C6, not '6 [?]'.
'X se factorise par Y∩Y' donc par un Z ∈ M, Z ≤ Y∩Y' ≤ Y, donc Z = Y (condition minimale)'; the line order in the transcription is scrambled.
Last line: 'et par suite Y ≤ Y'' is probably intended; the image appears to show 'Y = Y''.
